notes: Sign in as admin with the generated password. The admin is created on the first start (server --quick-init with ADMIN_USERNAME and ADMIN_PASSWORD); changing ADMIN_PASSWORD later does not change an existing admin, use the admin pages for that.
Nothing is public: PUBLIC_INDEX, PUBLIC_SNAPSHOTS and PUBLIC_ADD_VIEW are all False, so a logged-out visitor sees the login page, not the archive, and cannot add URLs.
The image is 0.7.4, the release upstream's stable tag points to. The 0.9 series is a rewrite with a different port (5797), a first-run setup wizard and new settings; it is not used here.
ALLOWED_HOSTS is the site's domain, so the app answers only for it. A domain change in the panel does not re-render this value; change ALLOWED_HOSTS in the environment to the new domain as well.
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS from the card is not set: it is not a setting in 0.7.4 (Django 3.1), and sign-in works over HTTPS without it.

Snapshots are taken by the Chromium, wget, yt-dlp and SingleFile extractors inside the container and stored in the data volume (/data) with the SQLite index. Upstream's default SAVE_ARCHIVE_DOT_ORG=True is kept, so every added URL is also submitted to the Internet Archive; set it to False in the environment for a fully private archive.
Chromium runs without its own sandbox (the 0.7 image's default in Docker), so the container needs no extra capability or security option.
